is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles sinensis, a malaria vector.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Rdl A296S (A296G/N/S), V327I, and T345S.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 provides genotype counts (AA/AS/SS, VV/VI/II, TT/TS/SS) for all seven populations.

african_field_population.evidence: The study populations are from Guangxi, China, along the China-Vietnam border. While the paper mentions imported malaria from Africa, the mosquitoes themselves are from China.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting new genotyping data for An. sinensis.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides specific sampling sites (villages) in Guangxi, China (e.g., Pingmeng, Xinwei, Tongde, Encheng, Shuikou, Shangshi, Dongxing).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Samples were collected from April 2015 to August 2017, which is a window of approximately 2.5 years.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study is a new survey of RDL mutations in An. sinensis, extending previous work on AChE and VGSC (Yang et al. 2019).

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including genotype counts, are provided in the main text tables.

assessment.summary: This study genotyped 208 Anopheles sinensis mosquitoes from seven locations along the China-Vietnam border for Rdl mutations (A296S, V327I, T345S). The study found high frequencies of the A296S mutation and reported genotype counts for all sites.
exclusion_reasons: The study populations are from China, not Africa.
